newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money eases, security prices harden.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money eases, security prices harden.

text.p: Indian call money eased on Thursday to below 11 percent while bond prices firmed up in brisk trade, dealers said.
They said call money was traded at 11.25 percent in opening deals but rates came down as demand eased.
"There was some early demand," said a dealer. "But later on borrowers became choosy and were not prepared to borrow above 11 percent..this brought rates down."
Dealers said prices of government securities moved up in brisk trade as market participants built up positions ahead of next week's cash reserve ratio cut (CRR).

"The CRR is to be cut to 10.5 percent from 11 percent on January 4," said a dealer. "Some players are building up positions ahead of this cut as they feel it will increase liquidity and rates will come down."
He said prices of securities moved up by 25-30 paise for securities maturing between 1998 and 2001.
